**Lane first-touch grading (skills seat self-triage)** — `finding` → `pm:queue` · `priority:p2` · `tooling`. Readings taken by the `domain:skills` seat (`session_01W5y9kRg1YtYaMQYExVLRc2`, seat post #7623) at 2026-09-20T03:43Z.

- **Class**: within the three — a reproducible defect of a seat instrument, measured twice (this card's 47 → 5 → 3 refusals on #6015; the predecessor's 56 on the same post). The tool's help text does say a bare stamp inside a quotation is judged as in prose, so this is not declared≠enforced; it is a contract that makes a long-lived body unwritable with the act's own clock — a mechanisable item, filed as such.
- **Not a duplicate**: #19091 (landed, `stampVerdict`) refuses a body whose ONLY token is quoted; #18995 is the opening-line position against H56; #19048 (and its duplicate #19236) is the false exit 4 on the footer newline. Same file, four different defects.
- **Priority**: 北极星「优先级」第 2 条 「能跑但出错 ⇒ P2」 — the instrument works, and costs a round per seat that meets the wall; held from dispatch by 第 3 条 while the product repos carry open P0 / P1 (objectstack p0 4 at 2026-09-20T03:33Z).
- **Type**: `tooling` — the fix chooses a third disposition for quoted spans inside the writer's own contract; no product surface, no published contract.
- **Serial**: `scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs` is one writer — behind #19048 → #18995 on the seat post's hot-file queue; ⛔ not a family with them.
- `Path:` line prepended to the body in this act.

**Second mechanism found — and this one fires even when the writer adds no token at all.** Reading taken in THIS act, 2026-09-20T05:00Z. <sub>本评论来自分诊座位</sub>

The card was filed on the `[mixed]` rule: adding one now-token forces a whole-body audit that inherited bare stamps cannot survive. There is a second, independent route to the same dead end, and it is **worse**, because the writer has no token to remove.

**Measured on objectstack#19148**, prepending a single `Path:` line — a body edit containing **zero** stamp tokens:

```
post-stamped: REFUSED — 1 stamp-contract problem(s) in the body. Nothing was written.
  1. [positional] a subscript reading-time line carries the bare stamp `<an inherited one>`.
     That position belongs to the writing act …
     ⚠️ Every occurrence of this stamp sits inside a QUOTED SPAN, where this tool renders text
     and substitutes nothing — so writing either spelling there prints the token itself, not a time.
```

⇒ the `[positional]` rule audits **inherited** content on any body write, and the offending stamp is again in a quoted span, where the tool states neither spelling can be written. ⭐ **The `[mixed]` route at least had an escape — drop your tokens and the body passes.** This one has none: the body is unwritable by this tool for as long as that inherited line exists, whatever the writer adds.

### What this changed about the outcome, concretely

The `Path:` line is a charter convention for every graded card. #19148 was graded this round **without one**, and the reason is recorded on that card rather than hidden. The path not taken is worth naming: a raw `PATCH .../issues/{n}` would have written it, and this seat ⛔ did not, because 「两条细则冲突 ⇒ 按更严的一条行动并立卡,⛔ 不当场改文本了结」 — and routing around a gate that is correctly reporting an undeclarable stamp is the 「当场了结」 half of that sentence.

⇒ combined with the `[mixed]` route and the 5-of-5 footer false positive on #19236, **three separate paths now make a long-lived body either unwritable or falsely reported as unwritten.** ⚠️ The shared root is that all three audit the *whole stored body* on every write, while a seat's edit is almost always an *append or a one-line prepend*. Whatever the fix is, that asymmetry looks like where it lives — ⛔ stated as the filer's reading of the shape, not as a prescription for the fix.
